newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian minfins weaker ahead of Greenspan address.
newsitem.headline: Russian minfins weaker ahead of Greenspan address.

text.p: Russian MinFins eased on foreign selling before Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's testimony, but Russian banks supported the market at lower levels, dealers said on Wednesday.
Greenspan testifies before the House of Rrepresentatives at 1900 GMT.
MinFin bonds, like Brady debt, are heavily influenced by moves in the U.S. Treasury bond market.

"New York was selling all Bradys and MinFins yesterday, and (the) closing was lower than in London," Mosbiznesbank dealer Igor Potapov said. "Russian banks started buying early today at attractive levels, but London prices went down again."
Brady bonds began falling on February 26 after Greenspan warned of inflation, which would mean higher interest rates. MinFins followed the global trend lower.

Dealers said the MinFin market was not jittery about a possible Russian cabinet reshuffle when President Boris Yeltsin delivers his state of the nation address to a joint parliamentary session on Thursday.

"We're not seeing any impact now since his speech is expected to be active and generally positive," Sberbank dealer pavel Sool said. "But the first market reaction to any government changes would be negative."
Dealers said the fourth, fifth and seventh tranches were hit the most, with some buying continuing on the local side.
